about: The collect of the prayers of Leo XIII said after low Mass, which follows the Salve Regína and its versicle. It asks God to look graciously upon the people who cry to Him and to hear the petitions offered through the intercession of the Blessed Virgin Mary, Saint Joseph, the Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the saints. It names two intentions: the conversion of sinners and the freedom and exaltation of the Church.

s02.translation: O God, our refuge and our strength, look with favor upon the people crying out to Thee;

s03.translation: and by the intercession of the glorious and immaculate Virgin Mary, Mother of God,

s04.translation: with blessed Joseph her Spouse, and Thy blessed Apostles Peter and Paul, and all the Saints,

s05.translation: the prayers we pour out for the conversion of sinners, for the freedom and exaltation of holy Mother Church,

s07.translation: Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

w001.function: A subjunctive expressing an exhortation to pray together.

w002.function: Vocative, identical here to the nominative.

w003.function: In apposition to “Deus” (w002). Refugium can denote both the act of taking refuge and a place of refuge. Here it names God.

w006.function: The second half of the apposition — “nostrum” (w004) covers both.

w011.function: A predicate adjective referring to the understood subject of “réspice” (w012).

w014.function: An ablative absolute with “Vírgine” (w018): the Virgin interceding.

w018.function: The noun of the ablative absolute. “intercedénte” (w014) and both adjectives agree with it.

w020.function: In apposition to “Vírgine” (w018), in the same case.

w022.function: A preposition beginning a separate phrase with the ablative.

w024.function: An indeclinable name, here in the ablative. One witness has “Josepho”, an inflection of “Iosephus”.

w025.function: The genitive of the demonstrative, pointing back to Mary in the line before.

w036.function: An adjective used substantivally: the saints.

w037.function: A feminine accusative plural relative pronoun. It refers to “preces” (w048), which appears later.

w048.function: The antecedent of “quas” (w037) and the object of “exáudi” (w053).

w049.function: Literally, we pour out. First person plural.

w052.function: A predicate adjective referring to the understood subject of “exáudi” (w053), as is “miséricors” (w050).

w055.function: The pronoun “eúndem” refers to the Son evoked earlier by the title “Genetríce” (w020) — Mother of God.
